title: turnstile-coordinator-graceful-eviction-and-hedge-timeouts
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Improve continuous batching scheduler robustness by introducing a turnstile coordinator that performs cooperative slot reshuffle, soft eviction grace, and hedged timeouts to reduce starvation and tail latency in mixed-KV workloads.
description: Motivation: In high-contention scenarios the continuous batcher can suffer from long tail latencies and starvation when KV-heavy requests pin slots for extended periods. Previous mitigations (soft reservation decay, probe-based backoff) reduced frequency of incidents but left pathological cases where a handful of long-running KV requests block progress for many short low-latency queries. This PR introduces a lightweight 'turnstile coordinator' that enables cooperative reshuffle of batch slots, implements a gracetime eviction window to avoid thrashing, and adds hedged timeout probes for suspected pin starvation. Summary of changes: 1) New turnstile_coordinator component in the batcher that tracks slot leases, last-progress timestamps, and a soft-priority score combining request age and estimated kv-cost; 2) Cooperative slot reshuffle: when a short request detects high slot hold time it can request a reshuffle token; the coordinator coordinates a fast, low-overhead swap of a pending short request into an available slot while ensuring in-flight KV operations are given a grace period; 3) Graceful eviction window: instead of hard preemption we mark targets for eviction and allow a bounded finish window (configurable) to commit or checkpoint state; 4) Hedged timeouts: short-path requests that exceed a per-queue dynamic threshold will spawn a single hedged probe to a warm replica/slot to reduce tail latency without significant duplicate work; hedging is rate-limited and respects cache affinity for KV operations; 5) Kernel hinting: scheduler heuristics expose a small hint API to the runtime kernels so they can prioritize progress of preemptable kernels (used for quantized KV helpers). Implementation details: Mostly in service/batcher/turnstile_coordinator.rs and service/batcher/slot_allocator.rs; small changes in runtime/kernel/sched_heuristics.cpp to add hinting hooks; KV-awareness in runtime/kv/cache_manager.cc to expose estimated pin-time for common ops; unit and integration tests added under tests/batcher. Performance: On a mixed workload synthetic benchmark (80% short inference calls, 20% KV-heavy long calls) we see median latency for short calls unchanged, p95 reduced by ~35% and p99 reduced by ~48% compared to baseline. CPU overhead is low (~2.1% median increase under peak throughput) and the hedging duplicate token rate stayed below 0.8% in experiments. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind batcher.turnstile.enabled; can be enabled for Canary fleet then ramped by region. Observability: new metrics added (batcher.turnstile.evictions, batcher.turnstile.hedged_probes, batcher.turnstile.reshuffle_requests) and tracing spans for coordinator operations. Backwards compatibility: default disabled to avoid changing existing behavior; safe toggles to tune grace window and hedging thresholds. Testing: added deterministic unit tests and end-to-end canary with failure injection (simulate long-pinning KV ops). Related work: builds on ENG-2389 (soft-reservation decay) and compliments ENG-2421 (probe coordinator). Security/compat: no secrets or surface area change. Caveats: in extremely adversarial synthetic load hedging can create duplicated KV reads; we cap hedged concurrency and added a knob to disable hedging per-customer for debug. TODO: add telemetry to correlate cache hit-rate with hedged effectiveness and expose an autosuggested grace window in Optimize. This PR is self-contained and small enough to roll back quickly via feature flag if unexpected regressions are observed.
